title: From Issue Number to Cabinet Address: Arthur C. Cole's Studies in Microscopical Science and the institutional re-addressing of published preparations
status: deep corpus delta complete; object-level provenance identity remains open

thesis_upgrade.previous: prepared slide -> published preparation -> later bibliographic disassembly
thesis_upgrade.revised: trade commodity -> published preparation -> institutional re-addressing -> selective recombination
thesis_upgrade.one_sentence: Cole synchronized specimen, image, method, issue number and subscription cadence to publish preparations; microscopical clubs then split, stored, renumbered and reclassified those components, converting serial time into cabinet order while retaining the possibility of recombining print and slide for display and study.
thesis_upgrade.definition: A preparation changes address when its operative retrieval identity moves from a commercial or serial coordinate to an institutional cabinet coordinate. This is more specific than generic circulation or decontextualization because the new address is an explicit retrieval system with its own maintenance logic.

croydon_1890_readdressing_system.source: Proceedings and Transactions of the Croydon Microscopical and Natural History Club, 1890 catalogue of microscopical preparations, corpus part 04
evidence: The catalogue says that little attempt has been made at scientific classification.
It explains that the collection is divided into 25 lettered sections in order to facilitate the introduction of new slides and the withdrawal of spoiled ones.
Members requesting slides must give the letter as well as the number of the slide.
The resulting address is therefore a two-part cabinet coordinate such as X48 or Y1 rather than an original publication number.
croydon_1890_readdressing_system.interpretation: The A-Z catalogue is a mutable maintenance and retrieval system. It privileges future insertion, withdrawal and finding over preservation of a slide's previous serial position.
croydon_1890_readdressing_system.claim_grade: S for stated design and address system; A+ for the interpretation as serial-to-cabinet re-addressing

croydon_1882_dedicated_cabinet.source: Croydon annual report for 1882, donations list
croydon_1882_dedicated_cabinet.evidence: A 'Cabinet for Slides illustrating Microscopical Studies' was presented by Mr W. F. Stanley.
croydon_1882_dedicated_cabinet.interpretation: A storage problem appeared at almost the same time as the hybrid publication: slides associated with 'Microscopical Studies' received a purpose-named cabinet rather than being treated merely as loose preparations.
croydon_1882_dedicated_cabinet.external_context: Independent slide-history research documents W. F. Stanley as a retailer of Arthur C. Cole preparations and illustrates an Arthur Cole slide carrying Stanley's retail label. This materially strengthens, but does not prove, the identification of the Croydon cabinet with Cole's serial.
croydon_1882_dedicated_cabinet.claim_grade: S for cabinet donation wording; A/A+ for direct identification with Cole's Studies
croydon_1882_dedicated_cabinet.guard: The Croydon wording itself says 'Microscopical Studies' rather than explicitly naming A. C. Cole. Do not promote the cabinet-to-Cole link to S without a contemporary accession label, minute, or surviving cabinet inscription.

quekett_bifurcation_reframed.evidence: The completed printed volume is listed among Library additions while the specimens accompanying Cole's Studies are separately described as possessed by subscription in the Cabinet section.
quekett_bifurcation_reframed.interpretation: Bibliographic disassembly was a managed transition from synchronized receipt to bifurcated custody. The distinction between Library and Cabinet acted on the mixed publication after acquisition.
quekett_bifurcation_reframed.claim_grade: S for separate placement; A+ for institutional-remediation interpretation

leicester_recombination.evidence: Several numbers of Cole's periodical, coloured figures and accompanying slides were exhibited together.
leicester_recombination.interpretation: Institutional or personal separation was reversible. The hybrid publication could be spatially recomposed for public viewing.
leicester_recombination.claim_grade: S for co-display; A+ for recombination interpretation

contrast_with_serial.serial_coordinate: fixed issue sequence organized by publication cadence and subject track
contrast_with_serial.cabinet_coordinate: mutable letter-number retrieval position organized for collection maintenance

infrastructure_transformations.name: trade
infrastructure_transformations.evidence: Cole & Son sold prepared slides through a wider optician network before Studies.

infrastructure_transformations.name: serial publication
infrastructure_transformations.operative_address: issue number + page + plate + distributed preparation
infrastructure_transformations.evidence: Studies synchronized a specimen, prose, method/bibliography and image in a recurring subscription.

infrastructure_transformations.name: subscriber collection
infrastructure_transformations.evidence: Volume II sends readers back to previously issued numbered slides, making the accumulated objects navigable as a collection.

infrastructure_transformations.name: institutional bifurcation
infrastructure_transformations.evidence: Quekett records the completed volume in its Library while retaining accompanying preparations in its Cabinet.

infrastructure_transformations.name: cabinet reclassification
infrastructure_transformations.operative_address: letter + number, e.g. Y1 or X48
infrastructure_transformations.evidence: Croydon's 1890 catalogue explicitly designs its system for insertion, withdrawal and retrieval.

infrastructure_transformations.name: recombination
infrastructure_transformations.evidence: Leicester display evidence puts numbers of the periodical, coloured figures and slides together again.

argument_payoff.strongest_new_sentence: At Croydon, publication numbers ceased to be operative addresses; preparations were assigned new cabinet coordinates.
argument_payoff.second_sentence: Serial order fixed an object to a publication sequence, whereas cabinet order was deliberately mutable, built to admit new slides and withdraw spoiled ones.
argument_payoff.third_sentence: The afterlife of the mixed serial was therefore not simple loss: institutions actively translated one retrieval system into another.
argument_payoff.historiographical_value: This shifts the case from a curiosity about books supplied with objects toward a history of how material publications are made bibliographically legible, then made administratively legible again under different collection regimes.

revised_article_architecture.title: Selling Preparations
revised_article_architecture.claim: Cole entered the serial venture from an established commercial market in prepared slides.

revised_article_architecture.title: Publishing Preparations
revised_article_architecture.claim: The serial synchronized two interleaved subject tracks and coupled object, prose, image, method and cadence.

revised_article_architecture.title: Unequal Copies
revised_article_architecture.claim: Subscriber specimens varied and mounting could distort them, so print calibrated and corrected the material edition.

revised_article_architecture.title: From Issue Number to Cabinet Number
revised_article_architecture.claim: Quekett and Croydon show two successive forms of institutional remediation: categorical splitting and explicit re-addressing.

revised_article_architecture.title: Recomposing the Publication
revised_article_architecture.claim: Exhibition and study could reunite print, image and slide, showing that the publication's components remained relational even after storage systems separated them.

guards: Do not identify Croydon's 1882 Stanley cabinet as definitively Cole's until an explicit contemporary or surviving-object link is found.
Do not treat exact subject matches as specimen identity. Repeated professional preparations could exist outside the subscription series.
Do not infer maker attribution from visually implied ditto marks in OCR without page-image collation.
Y1 Pikrite is currently the strongest provenance candidate because subject, locality and maker all match; it still lacks a subscription-specific mark.
Do not force X74 Rat Spermatozoa into Studies merely because Cole is explicit in the maker column.
Do not describe re-addressing as simple decontextualization. The new catalogue creates a functional context optimized for institutional retrieval and maintenance.
Do not describe later recombination as restoration of an original complete copy unless the exhibited slides can be proven to be the same issue copies.
